title: kv-cache: defragmentation + paging + spillover heuristics for improved memory usage and stability
author: Evan Brooks
description: Motivation: KV cache memory fragmentation and unbounded resident memory during high-concurrency workloads was causing OOMs and unpredictable latency. This PR implements a multi-pronged memory management strategy: (1) online defragmentation of the GPU-resident KV allocator to reduce fragmentation-induced capacity loss, (2) transparent paging of cold KV shards to host memory with async prefetch on hot access, and (3) heuristic spillover rules that proactively demote low-reuse entries when memory pressure is detected. The changes include allocator instrumentation, new eviction policy (LRU-window with reuse scoring), background defrag worker, host-paging layer with tunable thresholds, and scheduler hints so the request router can prefer warmed workers. We include microbenchmarks and end-to-end load tests showing 18-32% reduction in average resident memory under synthetic high-concurrency chat workloads and 6-12% lower p99 latency for long-context prompts due to reduced OOM/GC events. Rollout plan: staged canary on Dedicated then gradual ramp to hosted with telemetry gating. Backout: feature flag to disable paging/defrag and revert to previous eviction policy. The description below summarizes the key changes, tests, and known limitations.

merge_summary: Merged by squash merge. Squash commit summarizes defrag + paging + heuristic eviction changes. Rollout gated by feature flag and telemetry. Post-merge: created a follow-up to tune host-paging thresholds based on production signals.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: online defragmentation, host paging for cold shards, and new reuse-weighted eviction heuristics; reduces GPU resident memory usage and stabilizes long-running workers; feature-gated rollout.
known_limitations: Host paging adds tail latency under extreme host-memory pressure; mitigated by prefetch/backpressure but still requires tuning per-region
Defrag worker can increase temporary memory spikes during compaction windows; tuning knobs provided
Policy parameters are conservative defaults; long-tail workloads may need cust-specific tuning
benchmarks_summary: Microbenchmarks: 18-32% reduction in resident memory under synthetic high-concurrency workloads. E2E: 6-12% p99 latency improvement for long-context prompts due to fewer OOM/GC events. See benchmarks/kv_cache/concurrency_load.py for scripts and raw data stored in perf-canary artifacts.
